page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4-lssd is a general-purpose server instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 1:4 resource ratio. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. This processor configuration includes 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, utilizing dedicated CPU allocation. The CPU cache architecture consists of a 48 KB L1 data cache, a 2 MB L2 cache, and a 105 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

This instance comes bundled with a 402 GB local NVMe SSD, providing high-speed local storage. In benchmark evaluations, the server exhibits average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1617.89 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1714.0. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 3323.04 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 3812.0. Memory performance also falls into the lower tier, with uncached large-block read bandwidth at 29.2 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 22.26 GB/sec.

Given its hardware profile, the c3-standard-4-lssd offers a cost-efficient balance for workloads requiring fast local storage but moderate compute density. It is well-suited for static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 6.5 GB/sec, and single-threaded data processing tasks like gzip compression. However, due to its weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks, it is less optimal for heavy multi-threaded compilation, database operations, or large-scale LLM inference.
